newsitem.title: UK: IBCA rates Portugal AA minus long-term sovereign.
newsitem.headline: IBCA rates Portugal AA minus long-term sovereign.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating, said on Thursday it had assigned the Republic of Portugal a AA minus long-term sovereign credit rating.
This is the first formal sovereign rating of the country, IBCA said in a statement.
"The rating applies to some $12.9 billion of senior and unsecured foreign currency debt obligations of the Republic of Portugal and to its fully guaranteed issues," IBCA said.
"It will also serve as a ceiling for the borrowing in foreign currency of Portuguese banks and other issuers."

"The long-term foreign currency rating replaces the implicit sovereign assessment of AA minus that had previously acted as the ceiling for borrowing in foreign currency of Portuguese banks and other IBCA rated issuers," the rating agency said.
IBCA said the AAA local currency sovereign rating applied to debt worth 9,107.1 billion escudos ($59.6 billion).

"The rating reflects the swift modernisation that has taken place in the Portuguese economy since its accession to the European Union in 1986. The government has implemented a high degree of structural reform (notably privatisation), and inflation has fallen steadily while coupled with relatively high growth," IBCA said. "These factors have resulted in an increase in Portuguese living standards which have now reached 70 percent of the EU level."
The agency said Portugal's accession had led to an inflow of transfers which were utilised for infrastructure projects, and inflows of foreign direct investment.

"Foreign direct investment has allowed a diversification in exports away from the more traditional leather goods and textiles. However, a concern is that the reduction in foreign direct investment over the last few years, reflecting both the recession across the EU and the diversion of investment to the eastern European economies, will slow the convergence," it said.
"Unemployment is not a serious problem in Portugal at present but there are some fears that a structural element may be developing."

"Although Portugal has yet to establish a long track record in sound fiscal management, recent performance has been impressive and contributes to the positive outlook for the rating," IBCA said. "The general government deficit as a percentage of GDP is set to have come in below target in 1996, and should meet the Maastricht criterion in 1997. While the debt to GDP ratio will fall outside the Maastricht limit and there is a risk that the same will happen with inflation, Portugal stands a better chance than other southern Europeans of early membership of monetary union in 1999."

IBCA said the political outlook was stable, as both the centre-left Socialist Party (which won the 1995 election) and the centre-right Social Democratic Party had an objective to increase the integration of the Portuguese economy with its EU partners.
"Thus there is a general consensus on macro-economic policy," IBCA said.
